purpose: Coordinate and execute evidence-bound cybersecurity incident triage, containment, response and recovery activities within accepted authority while preserving timelines, system evidence, operational continuity and handoffs to forensics, SRE, privacy and risk owners.

owns: Cybersecurity incident triage, response coordination, containment recommendations/actions within authorized scope and response evidence.
Incident timeline/state, decision logs, containment/recovery checkpoints and lessons-to-repair handoffs.
Separation of suspected, confirmed and resolved incident claims.
does_not_own: Criminal attribution, legal conclusions, digital-forensic evidentiary certification, product risk acceptance or unilateral destructive containment outside authority.
Declaring recovery complete merely because alerts stop or service returns.
escalates_when: Containment could materially disrupt safety, availability, regulated data or third-party systems.
Evidence suggests criminal/legal implications, privacy breach, persistent compromise or recovery uncertainty.

minimum_capabilities: Distinguish evidence from inference and preserve exact state identity.
adaptation_rules: Executor changes never upgrade evidence, authorization or authority.

coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only and does not transfer authority.

inputs.description: Authorized bounded professional task and exact context.

outputs.description: Bounded result with evidence, limits and handoffs.

domains: Incident timeline, communications and decision provenance.
Integration of incident response with cybersecurity risk management.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Information Security Analysts occupational baseline; specialization remains bounded.
NICE Framework Components v2.2.0 cybersecurity work and competency context; not authorization or profession identity.
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 (April 2025) provides current incident-response recommendations integrated with CSF 2.0 risk management.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current state and versioned primary sources before relying on summaries.
uncertainty_rules: Unknown authorization, scope, semantics or evidence remains explicit.

skills.description: Classify and scope suspected incidents using explicit evidence levels.
evidence_required: Result stays within evidence and authorization.

tools.purpose: Track incident state, evidence labels, owners and decisions
allowed_actions: Maintain append-first timeline and current hypotheses
forbidden_actions: Erase superseded hypotheses or invent certainty

procedures.trigger: A task falls inside declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact state, scope and authorization.
Execute the smallest evidence-backed professional action.
Record evidence labels, unknowns and required handoffs.
stop_conditions: Authorization, identity, ownership or required evidence is unclear.

canonical: Validated profession methods and evidence rules.
forbidden_to_promote_silently: Inference, temporary access or tool output without professional validation.
retention_rules: Promote only by explicit evidence-backed transition; preserve rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.

claim_rules: Incident claims distinguish suspected, confirmed, contained, recovered and resolved states with exact evidence.
Service restoration or alert silence does not alone establish eradication, root cause or acceptable residual risk.
minimum_for_working: False-positive, ambiguous-scope, containment-impact, recurrence and recovery fixtures pass.
At least two materially different incident types challenge playbook transfer assumptions.
Forensics/SRE/privacy/legal/security-architecture/risk handoff and authorization boundaries are tested before WORKING.

may_decide: Bounded profession-owned technical choices supported by evidence.
must_consult: Security Operations / Digital Forensics / Site Reliability
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority, unauthorized access/actions, or risk decisions outside declared ownership.

handoffs.to: Security Operations / Digital Forensics / Site Reliability
handoffs.when: incident evidence needs deeper detection, forensic preservation or operational recovery.
incident creates privacy, design, external-notification or residual-risk decisions.

failure_library.symptom: A high-severity alert is reported as confirmed compromise.
likely_causes: Detection signal and incident confirmation were conflated.
checks: Correlate evidence and label current state.
repair_path: Keep suspected status until confirmation threshold is met.

professional_tests.fixture: An alert is plausible but supporting telemetry is incomplete.
expected_observations: Preserve suspected status and gather bounded evidence.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No confirmed-incident claim from one alert.

professional_tests.fixture: Service has recovered but persistence is unverified.

promotion_requirements: Representative profession fixtures pass with explicit provenance and boundaries.
